title: New Jersey AI Laws

reading.body:
New Jersey's only AI-related law targets rent-setting software, not AI in general, and it treats algorithmic price coordination as an antitrust violation.

The law, A3497, passed on 2026-07-20 and is named the Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent Act. It makes it unlawful for rental property owners to use coordinators that perform coordinating functions, for coordinators to facilitate agreements among owners that restrict competition, and for two or more persons to engage in parallel pricing coordination. It also bars any person from performing a coordinating function, defines algorithmic device, coordinating function, and competitively sensitive information, and requires the Attorney General to establish a complaint location and authorizes rulemaking.

This is a competition statute rather than an AI safety or transparency statute. It reaches the software only through the conduct it enables, which means the compliance question for a landlord or a pricing vendor is whether the tool coordinates behavior across parties, not whether it uses AI. That framing matters for compute because algorithmic rent coordination runs on ordinary cloud infrastructure, so the law constrains a business practice rather than the data centers or power that would host it.

The data covers one law and nothing else. It does not say how many AI-related bills New Jersey has introduced, how many failed, whether other laws touch AI without being classified that way, or how the Attorney General's complaint process will work in practice. It also does not establish that this is the state's full AI regulatory posture, only the count this site judged relevant.

New Jersey has enacted 1 AI-related law. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in New Jersey

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • A3497: Establishes "Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act." passed 2026-07-20

    The act makes it unlawful and a violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act for rental property owners to use coordinators that perform coordinating functions, for coordinators to facilitate agreements among rental property owners that restrict competition, for two or more persons to engage in parallel pricing coordination, and for any person to perform a coordinating function. It defines key terms such as algorithmic device, coordinating function, and competitively sensitive information. It requires the Attorney General to establish a complaint location and authorizes rulemaking.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for New Jersey. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
